Change.description:
One remote-originated change since the caller's cursor. The plugin maps
each to the corresponding VFileEvent and a VirtualFile.refresh() call.

old_path.description: Required for kind in (rename, move). The plugin uses (old_path -> path) to fire VFilePropertyChangeEvent(PROP_NAME)/VFileMoveEvent and keep the open editor's identity, instead of a delete+create that would invalidate it.
old_path.title: Old Path

path.description: New/current path of the affected node.
path.title: Path

requestor.description: Null if externally originated; set if this echoes a plugin-initiated op.
requestor.title: Requestor

stable_id.description: Identity key; ties a rename/move's old and new paths to one node.
stable_id.title: Stable Id

Change.title: Change

ChangesSinceResponse.description:
Cursor-paginated. The plugin's background poller calls this on an
interval (the same poll discussed for local_modified_at, just over HTTP)
and replays the changes into the platform on the EDT in a write action.

next_cursor.description: Opaque; pass back as `cursor` on the next poll.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

ChangesSinceResponse.title: ChangesSinceResponse

Commit.description:
Outbound log -- one row per attempted push back to the wiki. Kept as a log
(not an in-place overwrite of Page.revid) so a rejected edit-conflict attempt
is visible and retriable rather than silently lost, and the IDE can show
"this save failed, here's why" after the fact.
Commit.title: Commit

handled.description: Number of pages whose pending local edits were pushed this run.
handled.title: Handled

EditJournal.description:
Local transaction log of IDE saves, kept distinct from the cached remote
body. Every VFS write appends a row (and flips Page.dirty); a commit reads
the uncommitted rows, pushes via pywikibot, and marks them committed. This
is what keeps "save in the IDE" cheap/offline and separate from "push to the
wiki".
EditJournal.title: EditJournal

FetchRequest.description:
The cache-fill queue (out-of-band, "git checkout" path). The plugin
INSERTs; the pywikibot worker claims pending rows, updates status/progress,
and fans out children for an Index (parent_pk) so the plugin can watch
aggregate progress on the one request it submitted.
FetchRequest.title: FetchRequest

FileBlob.description:
Stat-like record for a downloaded File: binary.

Tracks what pywikibot's FileInfo / MediaWiki imageinfo API returns for a
specific file revision, plus the local path of the downloaded blob.  The
VFS uses this to answer stat/HEAD requests without re-reading the file.

``file_sha1`` is the SHA1 of the binary payload -- distinct from the
wikitext revision sha1 on Page and the correct cache-key for the blob.
A new revision of the file gets a new row (or an upsert of the fields).
FileBlob.title: FileBlob

Namespace.description:
Per-site namespace map, populated from each wiki's ``siteinfo``. Lets a
Page from a 250-wiki and a Page from a 104-wiki be recognised as the same
kind of object.
Namespace.title: Namespace

Node.description:
One entry as the VFS sees it. `stable_id` is the rename-survival key
(MediaWiki pageid) -- distinct from `path`, which changes on rename.

content_model.description: Remote contentmodel (e.g. 'proofread-index', 'proofread-page', 'sanitized-css', 'json'). None for directories/synthetic nodes.
content_model.title: Content Model

length.description: Content length in bytes; None for directories.
length.title: Length

path.description: wikisource://-relative path, uniquely identifies the node
path.title: Path

revid.description: Revision id as of last fetch; the conflict token.
revid.title: Revid

stable_id.description: MediaWiki pageid; survives renames. None until first remote fetch.
stable_id.title: Stable Id

timestamp.description: Drives VirtualFile.getTimeStamp(). Reflects local_modified_at, NOT remote revision time -- see schema model notes.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

Node.title: Node

NsRole.description:
Portable namespace role. Numeric namespace ids are per-site (Page=104 on
en.wikisource, 250 on a fresh ProofreadPage reinstall; Book is operator-
chosen), so we never compare ids across wikis -- we compare roles. A role is
resolved from the *canonical* namespace name, which is stable everywhere.
NsRole.title: NsRole

Page.description:
One (site, title) object -- mainspace, Index:, Page:, Book:, anything.
One table, not three: "search/replace across the whole work" is a core use
case and wants a single scan. The namespace role discriminates shape;
role-specific columns are nullable and only meaningful for their role.

(site_pk, title) is the natural key. pageid/revid are wiki-local and not
comparable across independently-running instances -- which is exactly why
this can't be ``pageid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY``.
Page.title: Page

requestor.description: Echoed back on the resulting change-feed entry so the plugin can tell its own initiated rename from an externally-detected one (null requestor == external change, mirroring VFS getRequestor() semantics).
requestor.title: Requestor

Site.description:
One MediaWiki instance. Identity is the pywikibot (family, code) pair --
that is the request vocabulary (``title:x family:y code:z``) and what
pywikibot itself keys on. ``host``/``api_url`` are derived/optional, never the
key, because pageids/revids from two independent wikis are not comparable.
Site.title: Site

SiteCredential.description:
Per-site login credential. Deliberately separate from the Site row so
Site rows are safe to inspect and log without leaking secrets. The password
field is plaintext -- acceptable for a local single-user dev tool; the DB
lives in the same process-local directory as the pywikibot config.
SiteCredential.title: SiteCredential

StatBulkResponse.description: Same order as the request's `paths` -- index i answers paths[i].
StatBulkResponse.title: StatBulkResponse

base_revid.description: Revid the edit is based on -- sent as basetimestamp/conflict token. A mismatch against current remote state is an edit conflict, surfaced as WriteResult.status='conflict', not an error.
base_revid.title: Base Revid

get.description: VFS getChildren(). Pure cache reads — never triggers a wiki fetch.

post.description:
Local save only -- appends an EditJournal row and updates the cached
Page.text. Does not touch the wiki; that happens later when the commit
worker drains uncommitted journal rows via pywikibot.

Batched stat() for refresh() sweeps over many cached paths at once.

Page-under-Pages/ paths (the dominant case at real-library scale — one
query per site+index_title rather than one per page) are batched via
`Page.title.in_(...)`; every other path shape falls back to `_stat_one`,
since sites/indexes/file-dirs are comparatively few per session.

schema.title: Response List Index Pages Viewer Indexes Get
